summary: @onereach/v-event-calendar preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the extracted binary executable, and then invokes it against a shipped sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB Bun-compiled blob (leading `// @bun @bun-cjs` marker) obfuscated with a numeric/string constant array plus a rotation function (`WV8StW`, classic string-array-shift obfuscator). The `setup.mjs` loader itself is obfuscated in the obfuscator.io style (hex-named identifiers, dispatch objects mapping short keys to `execFileSync`, `readFileSync`, `/etc/os-release`, `ldd`, `bun`, `--version`, `Alpine`). The package's advertised purpose is a Vue event-calendar component, which does not require an alternate JavaScript runtime or a large opaque binary blob. The Bun runtime is fetched purely to execute the obfuscated sibling payload out of view of Node-based scanners, giving the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer machine on `npm install`. File and behavior naming (`math_init.js` inside a calendar package) does not correspond to any documented functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
